title: MemogentAI (FiscalFlow)
text: MemogentAI, also known as FiscalFlow, is an AI-powered financial due diligence product from Excel databooks. I built an Excel-first ingest and RAG pipeline that audits spreadsheets, extracts tables, and indexes evidence. Orchestrated multi-section FDD report generation with LangChain and LangGraph: plan, draft, persona review, and quality gates. Designed human-in-the-loop approve / edit / reject interrupts. Desktop client: React + Tauri (fiscalflow-ui) with a looping demo walkthrough plus screenshots of home, workspace, settings, and Excel Auditor review. API: fiscalflow-api. Repo: https://github.com/FiscalFlowHQ/fiscalflow-ui

title: MemogentAI: Desktop Workspace
text: Tauri + React run UI: upload databooks, watch SSE progress on a pipeline rail, review drafts and evidence, then export Markdown / PPTX / PDF.

title: MemogentAI: API Gateway
text: FastAPI sessions and documents over REST, plus SSE streams. Pure transport: the graph owns generation; the API validates, streams, and resumes HITL.

title: MemogentAI: Ingest & RAG
text: Audit Excel for reference errors, extract tables into a structured catalog, then embed chunks into a local LanceDB hybrid store (dense + BM25).

title: MemogentAI: Document Orchestrator
text: Outer LangGraph on LangChain: global plan, sequential section loop, cross-section review, and final document assembly with durable state keyed by thread.

title: MemogentAI: Section Engine
text: Inner chain per section: retrieve → compress evidence → outline → draft → multi-persona critique → polish → claims → quality gate.

title: MemogentAI: Human-in-the-Loop
text: Gated plan and review interrupts at global, section, and step tiers. One resume contract: approve, edit, or reject, then the stream continues.

title: LAAM Analytics
text: LAAM Analytics is a buyer-behaviour analytics product for a fashion marketplace. I built a Django and DRF API that computes every aggregate in SQLite — sales over time, top products and brands, and frequently-bought-together co-occurrence with confidence and lift — so the browser never receives raw order rows. The React Vite dashboard has composable filters, brand drill-down, pagination, and a product-insights drawer. I added LocMem caching, Docker Compose, measured EXPLAIN query plans, and 122 backend tests. Public repo: https://github.com/ansab-rehman/buyer-analytics

title: Skills used in LAAM Analytics
text: LAAM Analytics used Django and Django REST Framework for the API, parameterized SQLite SQL for all aggregation, React with Vite and TypeScript for the UI, TanStack Query for data fetching, Recharts for charts, LocMem response caching, and Docker Compose with nginx. Core skills on display: server-side analytics, date-range edge cases, market-basket analysis (confidence and lift), pagination, query-performance thinking with EXPLAIN plans, and clean full-stack delivery.

title: LAAM Analytics: frequently bought together
text: In LAAM Analytics I implemented market-basket analysis for a selected product: same-order co-occurrence ranked like the reference SQL, plus confidence and lift so bestsellers do not fake affinity. The insights drawer also shows how many customers bought the product. Aggregation stays in SQL on the server.
